entities.name: Princely Church Saint Nicholas Curtea de Argeș
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Princely Church of Saint Nicholas (Romanian: Biserica Domnească Sfântul Nicolae din Curtea de Argeș) in Curtea de Argeș, Romania, is a 14th-century Orthodox church built by the Wallachian prince Basarab I (founder of the Wallachian principality) circa 1352 — one of the oldest surviving medieval Christian buildings in Romania and a monument to the founding of the Wallachian state, which would eventually become part of modern Romania. The church stands near the famous 16th-century Curtea de Argeș Monastery (Cathedral) that is the burial site of Romanian royalty.

Basarab I of Wallachia (ruled circa 1310-1352) was the founder of the independent Wallachian principality — the first independent Romanian state — following his victory over Hungarian forces at the Battle of Posada (1330). The Princely Church of Saint Nicholas, constructed toward the end of his reign, was the religious expression of the new state's independence and its Orthodox Christian identity. Wallachia's Orthodoxy (in contrast to Catholic Hungary and Poland to its north and west) was a defining cultural characteristic that aligned it with the Byzantine tradition and with Serbia and Bulgaria.

The church's Byzantine-influenced architectural style, with its frescoes (some original 14th-century work surviving alongside later restorations), documents the artistic and religious connections between Wallachia and the broader Orthodox Christian world of the 14th century. Curtea de Argeș (literally 'Argeș Court') was the first capital of independent Wallachia, making the church a site of Romanian state origins. The later Curtea de Argeș Monastery (built 1512-1517) would house the tombs of Romanian kings.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Princely Church of Saint Nicholas Curtea de Argeș — built by Basarab I, founder of Wallachia (the first independent Romanian state), Romania's oldest surviving medieval church, and the founding religious monument of Romanian Orthodox statehood — is one of Romania's most historically significant medieval monuments.
